legal.privacy.title: Privacy Policy
legal.privacy.intro: Trakwyn (“Trakwyn”, “we”, “us”) helps you track job applications, interviews, and offers. This policy explains what information we collect, how we use it, and the choices you have.
legal.privacy.accountBody: When you create an account, we collect your email address and a password (stored as a salted hash — we never see or store your password in plain text). You may optionally add your name, timezone, and target role.
legal.privacy.oauthBody: If you sign in with Google or GitHub instead, we receive your name, email address, and a profile identifier from that provider. We never see your Google or GitHub password.
legal.privacy.jobDataBody: Everything you enter to track your job search: applications (company, role, status, notes), contacts, interview rounds, offers, and any documents (résumés, cover letters, offer letters) you upload.
legal.privacy.securityInfoBody: To protect your account, we log the IP address, approximate location, and device/browser information associated with sign-ins and certain security-sensitive actions (password changes, two-factor authentication changes, session revocations). This is what powers “new device signed in” alerts and the active-sessions list in Settings.
legal.privacy.aiTitle: AI features, if you use them
legal.privacy.aiBody: Trakwyn’s AI features (cover letter generation, résumé matching, the assistant) are bring-your-own-key: you provide your own API key for a provider you choose (e.g. OpenRouter, Google AI). Your key is encrypted at rest. When you use an AI feature, the relevant content (e.g. a job description, your résumé text) is sent directly to the provider you configured — not stored or processed by any AI service of ours. That provider’s own privacy policy governs how they handle it.
legal.privacy.cookiesBody: We use cookies necessary to keep you signed in, which can’t be switched off, and, only where you’ve opted in, analytics cookies to understand how Trakwyn is used. You can review or change your choice anytime via “Cookie preferences” in the site footer.
legal.privacy.useOperate: To operate Trakwyn — storing and displaying the data you enter, keeping you signed in.
legal.privacy.useSecure: To secure your account — detecting unfamiliar sign-ins, supporting password resets and two-factor authentication.
legal.privacy.useEmail: To send account-related email — email verification, password reset, security alerts, and, if you’ve enabled it, a weekly or daily digest of your job search activity. You can turn optional emails off in Settings.
legal.privacy.useImprove: To fix bugs and improve the product, using aggregated, anonymized usage data.
legal.privacy.shareIntro: We do not sell your personal information. We share it only with:
legal.privacy.shareProvidersRest: who process it on our behalf to run Trakwyn — our hosting provider, our email delivery provider, and, only if you’ve configured them, the OAuth provider you sign in with and the AI provider you bring your own key for.
legal.privacy.shareLawRest: if required by law, or to protect the rights, property, or safety of Trakwyn, our users, or others.
legal.privacy.controlBody: You can export a full copy of your data, or permanently delete your account, at any time from Settings. Deleting your account is a hard delete — it removes your applications, documents, notes, and the security/login records described above, not a soft delete or deactivation. Once deleted, we cannot recover it.
legal.privacy.dataSecurityBody: Passwords are hashed, sensitive fields (like AI provider keys and two-factor secrets) are encrypted at rest, and account access supports two-factor authentication. No method of transmission or storage is 100% secure, but we work to protect your information using practices appropriate to the sensitivity of the data involved.
legal.privacy.childrenBody: Trakwyn is not directed at children, and we do not knowingly collect information from anyone under 16. If you believe a child has provided us information, contact us and we will delete it.
legal.privacy.changesBody: We may update this policy from time to time. If we make material changes, we’ll update the “Last updated” date above and, where appropriate, notify you directly.
legal.privacy.contactPrefix: Questions about this policy or your data? Email us at
legal.terms.title: Terms of Service
legal.terms.intro: These terms govern your use of Trakwyn. By creating an account or using Trakwyn, you agree to them. If you don’t agree, please don’t use Trakwyn.
legal.terms.serviceBody: Trakwyn is a job-search tracking tool: applications, interviews, offers, documents, and optional AI-assisted features. Trakwyn is currently provided free of charge. We may introduce paid plans in the future; if we do, this policy will be updated and you’ll be told before anything you’re using becomes paid.
legal.terms.accountAge: You must be at least 16 years old to use Trakwyn.
legal.terms.accountAccuracy: You’re responsible for the accuracy of the information you provide when registering.
legal.terms.accountSecurity: You’re responsible for keeping your password confidential and for all activity under your account. Tell us right away if you suspect unauthorized access — Settings lets you revoke sessions and enable two-factor authentication.
legal.terms.contentBodyPrefix: You own the applications, notes, documents, and other content you add to Trakwyn (“your content”). You grant us a limited license to store, process, and display your content solely to provide the service to you. We don’t use your content to train AI models, and we don’t share it except as described in the
legal.terms.contentByokBody: If you use a bring-your-own-key AI feature, you’re responsible for complying with your chosen AI provider’s own terms and for any costs they charge you directly — Trakwyn does not bill you for AI usage and is not a party to your agreement with that provider.
legal.terms.acceptableLawful: Use Trakwyn for anything unlawful, or to violate anyone else’s rights.
legal.terms.acceptableAccess: Attempt to gain unauthorized access to Trakwyn, other users’ accounts, or our systems.
legal.terms.acceptableScrape: Scrape, reverse-engineer, or interfere with Trakwyn's operation.
legal.terms.acceptableMalicious: Upload malicious code or content that infringes someone else’s intellectual property.
legal.terms.terminationBody: You can delete your account at any time from Settings — this is a permanent, hard delete of your data, not a deactivation. We may suspend or terminate your access if you violate these terms, with notice where reasonably possible.
legal.terms.disclaimersBody: Trakwyn is provided “as is,” without warranties of any kind, express or implied. We don’t guarantee the service will be uninterrupted, error-free, or that any AI-generated content (cover letters, résumé feedback, and similar) will be accurate or suitable for your purposes — always review AI-generated content before relying on it.
legal.terms.liabilityBody: To the fullest extent permitted by law, Trakwyn and its operators are not liable for any indirect, incidental, or consequential damages arising from your use of the service, or for the accuracy of AI-generated content or third-party AI providers you’ve chosen to connect.
legal.terms.changesBody: We may update these terms from time to time. If we make material changes, we’ll update the “Last updated” date above and, where appropriate, notify you directly. Continuing to use Trakwyn after a change means you accept the updated terms.
legal.terms.contactPrefix: Questions about these terms? Email us at
legal.accessibility.title: Accessibility
legal.accessibility.intro: We want Trakwyn to be usable by everyone, including people using assistive technology like screen readers, keyboard-only navigation, or browser zoom.
legal.accessibility.targetBodySuffix: at Level AA. This is a target we’re working toward, not a certification — Trakwyn hasn’t had a full manual accessibility audit, so we can’t claim to have fully met it yet.
legal.accessibility.scansLi: Automated accessibility scans (axe-core) run in our test suite against key pages, including sign-in, registration, the dashboard, and the applications list, and are required to pass with zero violations before a change ships.
legal.accessibility.fixedLi: Accessibility issues found this way have been fixed as they were found.
legal.accessibility.limitationsBody: Our automated coverage doesn’t yet reach every page, and automated scans only catch a subset of real accessibility issues — they don’t replace testing with actual assistive technology. If you run into something that doesn’t work well with a screen reader, keyboard navigation, or another assistive tool, we want to know about it.
legal.accessibility.contactPrefix: Found an accessibility barrier, or have feedback on how we can do better? Email us at

guides.aiMcpSetup.title: Connect your own AI key and an MCP client
guides.aiMcpSetup.description: Bring your own provider key so AI features run on your account instead of a shared one, and connect an external app to read and update your Trakwyn data directly. Both are optional, and both are set up from inside the product once you're signed in.
guides.aiMcpSetup.part1Heading: Part 1 — Bring your own AI key
guides.aiMcpSetup.whatBody: Trakwyn's AI features — parsing job descriptions, drafting cover letters, matching your resume to a role, company briefings, and the chat assistant — call out to a large language model. With BYOK, that call uses an API key you generate on your own account with a provider like OpenAI or Anthropic, instead of a key Trakwyn manages for everyone.
guides.aiMcpSetup.costBody: Usage is billed by the provider straight to your own account — Trakwyn never sees the charge and adds nothing on top. Check your provider's pricing page for per-request cost.
guides.aiMcpSetup.storageBody: Your key is encrypted at rest and only decrypted on the server, in the moment it's needed to make a request on your behalf. It's never sent to your browser after you save it, and never shown again — if you lose track of it, remove it and add it again.
guides.aiMcpSetup.addStep1: Create a key with your chosen provider — see the note below the tabs for where.
guides.aiMcpSetup.addStep2: Sign in to Trakwyn and go to Settings → AI.
guides.aiMcpSetup.addStep3: Paste in the key and save. The model field is optional for every provider except a custom endpoint, where it — and a base URL — are both required.
guides.aiMcpSetup.providerCustomNote: Point Trakwyn at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint — a self-hosted model server, or another provider's compatibility layer.
guides.aiMcpSetup.expectTitle: What to expect the first time
guides.aiMcpSetup.expectBody: Today a key is only checked for the right shape when you save it, not tested against the provider. If it's wrong, expired, or out of credit, you'll find out the first time you use an AI feature, not at save time — that's what the error will mean if one shows up.
guides.aiMcpSetup.exposesBody: The Model Context Protocol lets an outside app — Claude Desktop, Cursor, or anything that speaks MCP — read your job-search data and, if you allow it, create or update it too. Nothing ever deletes: there are no delete tools at all.
guides.aiMcpSetup.readToolsBody: Applications, notes, interview rounds, contacts, work history, skills, documents, offers, activity, calendar, analytics.
guides.aiMcpSetup.writeToolsBody: Create or update applications, notes, interview rounds, skills, education, and work experience.
guides.aiMcpSetup.oauthIntro: The easiest way to connect a client — nothing to copy, paste, or manage. If your client supports OAuth, just point it at Trakwyn and it handles the rest:
guides.aiMcpSetup.oauthStep1: In your client, add Trakwyn as a remote MCP server using the server URL below.
guides.aiMcpSetup.oauthStep2: The client opens a sign-in window — sign in with your existing Trakwyn account, no separate step.
guides.aiMcpSetup.oauthStep3: Approve the consent screen, choosing Read-only or Full access — start with Read-only unless the client genuinely needs to create or update records.
guides.aiMcpSetup.oauthStep4: Done — the client is connected. Nothing to copy, and nothing to lose track of.
guides.aiMcpSetup.oauthRevoke: Revoking is all-or-nothing: taking back access from a client (below, or from within the client itself) invalidates everything that consent ever issued it, so it can't quietly refresh its way back in.
guides.aiMcpSetup.manageBody: Every client you've approved over OAuth is listed in Settings → Integrations, alongside your API tokens, where you can revoke access at any time.
guides.aiMcpSetup.configsClaudeCursorLab: Claude Desktop / Cursor — add as a remote server
guides.aiMcpSetup.configsClaudeCursorNot: The client opens a browser to sign in and consent the first time it connects — the exact key name may vary slightly by client version, so check its docs if this doesn't match.
guides.aiMcpSetup.tokenTitle: Advanced: connect with an API token
guides.aiMcpSetup.tokenIntro: For a script, a CI job, or a client that doesn't support OAuth — a long-lived token you paste into its config yourself.
guides.aiMcpSetup.tokenStep1: Sign in and go to Settings → Integrations.
guides.aiMcpSetup.tokenStep2: Name the token so you remember what it's for.
guides.aiMcpSetup.tokenStep3: Choose a scope — start with Read-only unless it genuinely needs to create or update records. A read-only token is refused by both the write tools and the API itself, so it can't change anything even if it leaks.
guides.aiMcpSetup.tokenStep4: Copy the token — it's shown once, right after you create it.
guides.aiMcpSetup.tokenCurlLabel: Generic JSON-RPC, with the token on the header

integrations.fallbackWhenLimitedLabel: Use another key when one hits its limit
integrations.fallbackWhenLimitedHelp: When the key an AI feature would use has reached its monthly token limit, fall through to your next key that still has room instead of stopping. You will be told which key answered. Off by default, because it spends money on a provider you did not pick for that task.
